# Pariññāvāra (Ya 7.2.4)

**ID:** Ya 7.2.4
**Section:** Yamaka (ya)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Pariññāvāra
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m5.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pariññāvāra* ("Section on Full Understanding" or "Penetration") is the fourth section of the *Anusayayamaka*, which constitutes the seventh treatise of the canonical Abhidhamma text *Yamaka* [Nyanatiloka 2007]. In the overall schema of the *Anusayayamaka*, it follows the section on abandoning biases (*pajahana-vāra*) and precedes the section on abandoned biases (*pahīna-vāra*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. More broadly across the *Yamaka*, the *pariññāvāra* represents one of the three standard structural divisions of Yamaka chapters, coming after the *paññattivāra* (delimitation of terms) and the *pavattivāra* (process) [Norman 1983; Anderson 1999; Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics]. In this division, the text systematically explores the extent to which a given individual or class of beings comprehends (*parijānāti*) the category under consideration, analyzing penetration (*pariññā*) as the penetrating insight attained at the stages of noble holiness [Nyanatiloka 2007; Norman 1983; Anderson 1999].

**Sources**

- [Nyanatiloka 2007] Nyanatiloka Mahāthera, Guide Through the Abhidhamma Pitaka (1938, rev. 2007) — Structural outline of the Anusayayamaka and definition of pariññā in the Yamaka.
- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pāli Literature (1983) — Account of the tripartite chapter structure of the Yamaka and scope of the Pariññāvāra.
- [Anderson 1999] Carol S. Anderson, Pain and Its Ending: The Four Noble Truths in the Theravāda Buddhist Canon (1999) — Analysis of the function and verbal framing (parijānāti) of the Pariññāvāra.
- [Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics] Noa Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics (2005) — Discussion of the three divisions (paññatti-vāra, pavatti-vāra, and pariññā-vāra) in Yamaka chapters.
